questions.question: What percentage of shoppers abandon their cart because they don't trust the site with payment info?
questions.answer_summary: About 19% of shoppers cite not trusting the site with credit card information as a reason for abandoning, per Baymard Institute research.

questions.question: Does requiring account creation increase cart abandonment?
questions.answer_summary: Yes — Baymard puts it around 18%, and Shopify's summary cites roughly a quarter of checkout abandonment being tied to forced account creation.

questions.question: How much does a complicated checkout process contribute to abandonment?
questions.answer_summary: Roughly 17-18% of abandonments are attributed to a checkout process being too long or complicated.

questions.question: How many form fields should an optimized checkout have?
questions.answer_summary: Average checkouts run around 23-24 form elements; Baymard's optimal-design research suggests this can be cut to roughly 12-14 without losing needed information.

questions.question: Does slow delivery time cause abandonment separately from shipping cost?
questions.answer_summary: Yes — about 20% of shoppers abandon specifically because delivery is too slow, distinct from the cost of shipping itself.

questions.question: Does an unclear returns policy cause cart abandonment?
questions.answer_summary: Yes — roughly 13-16% of abandonments are linked to dissatisfaction with the returns policy shown at checkout.

questions.question: Do website errors or crashes cause cart abandonment?
questions.answer_summary: Yes — technical problems like site errors during checkout account for about 17% of abandonments.

questions.question: Does a limited selection of payment methods cause cart abandonment?
questions.answer_summary: Yes — roughly 9-11% of shoppers abandon because their preferred payment method wasn't offered.

questions.question: Is cart abandonment worse on mobile than desktop?
questions.answer_summary: Yes — cited abandonment rates run roughly 85% on mobile versus about 73% on desktop and 80% on tablet.

questions.question: Does not being able to see the order total upfront cause abandonment?
questions.answer_summary: Yes — inability to see the full order cost before payment is cited as a distinct abandonment cause, around 12%.

questions.question: Does a declined credit card count as cart abandonment?
questions.answer_summary: Yes — it's tracked as its own distinct cause, around 10%, separate from a shopper voluntarily leaving.

questions.question: What's the difference between 'browsing abandonment' and 'checkout abandonment'?
questions.answer_summary: Browsing abandonment is leaving before starting checkout (often just comparison shopping); checkout abandonment is leaving after starting the payment flow, which is the more fixable segment that research on causes actually targets.
